abstract.t: The Mail Action Protocol (MAP) defines how a service describes an action in email, how an authorized client requests that action over HTTPS, and how the service reports and retains the result. MAP reuses the JSON-LD representation and MIME structure defined by the Structured Email work. It adds exact interaction-type, target, operation, authorization, idempotency, and recovery semantics. It does not replace email transport, grant service authority, or define a new agent identity system.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: Email routinely asks a recipient to act in another service: review a revision, supply information, respond to an event, or change a preference. A person can interpret the message and follow a link. An automated client needs a stable description of the operation, the exact object on which it acts, the service endpoint, and the possible outcomes.

MAP defines that interaction without moving business authority into email. The service remains authoritative for identity, permission, target state, additional approvals, and the operation's effect. The readable email and normal service interface remain available to a person.
The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, and MAY in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

section.name: Scope and Relationship to Existing Work
section.t: MAP descriptions are JSON-LD documents carried in an application/ld+json MIME part designated by Structured Email . SMTP, Internet Message Format, MIME, mailbox access, and provider APIs continue to perform their existing roles .

MAP 0.1 uses existing HTTPS and service authentication. It defines no custom DNS discovery, new media type, global identity provider, mandatory online registry lookup, or general permission-policy language. A later specification can define a different execution profile without changing email transport.

section.name: Structured Email Representation
section.t: A MAP message MUST contain readable content and exactly one application/ld+json part containing the MAP description. The structured part MUST carry Content-Purpose: Machine-readable. A receiver MUST NOT infer a MAP description from an undesignated JSON attachment.

A MAP action description represents part of a message. The sender MUST use multipart/related. The readable text and HTML variants, when both are present, remain a nested multipart/alternative part. The structured part MUST use base64 or quoted-printable content-transfer encoding.
A receiving system MAY extract and validate the description before it knows whether it will offer execution. Extraction and schema validation MUST NOT execute an operation or grant authority.

The structured value is ordinary JSON. JSON-LD expansion is optional. An implementation that expands the document MUST use the bundled profile context and MUST NOT retrieve a context named by an untrusted message.

dl.dd: The authority that owns an operation, checks permission, performs the effect, and records its result.
An agent, inbox, or application that reads a description and may submit an authorized request.
A versioned definition of the target, operations, inputs, results, and permission boundaries for a class of interaction.
The representation and execution rules used by one MAP exchange.
A service interface through which a person can inspect and complete the interaction.

section.name: Interaction Model
section.t: An interaction has three documents:

ol.li: A description identifies the profile, interaction type, service, exact target revision, offered operations, execution endpoint, result route, expiry, and human route.
A request repeats the exact interaction, type, operation, and target references and supplies type-specific input.
A result reports the authoritative state. A Problem Details document reports a request that was not applied.

section.t: The service MUST recheck authentication, authorization, target state, expiry, revocation, and any additional approval at execution time. Receiving or forwarding an email does not transfer permission.

section.name: Description
section.t: The MAP 0.1 profile URI is https://mailschema.org/profiles/map/0.1. A client MUST match this value exactly.

The field contract is the JSON Schema at https://mailschema.org/schemas/map-0.1.schema.json. A conforming profile release binds the exact schema and JSON-LD context bytes by SHA-256 digest; an implementation MUST NOT treat mutable content later retrieved from those URLs as the contract for an already supported profile. The principal members use the JSON data model :

dl.dd: A UUID URN identifying the interaction.
The interaction type URI, version, and exact canonical contract digest.
The service identity, HTTPS execution and result routes, human route, retention interval, and informational authentication metadata.
The service object, revision, and SHA-256 digest to which the operations apply.
Stable operation identifiers, readable labels, and type-specific input-schema references.

section.t: The description MUST NOT contain an access token, session credential, or new authorization grant. Its authentication metadata only names schemes that a configured client may already use.
A service MUST preserve the same interaction identifier when it redelivers the same underlying interaction. A changed target revision or changed set of offered operations is a new interaction.

section.name: Endpoint Trust
section.t: A description and every value derived from it are untrusted input. Before credential use, a client MUST match the service identity, exact HTTPS execution URL, result URL template, and credential audience against configuration obtained independently of the email. Matching only the origin is insufficient. Message authentication alone is also insufficient.

A client MUST apply the same checks to every redirect before sending a credential. A client MUST NOT automatically fetch or interpret an unknown schema, URL, or instruction named by the message. These rules align with the Structured Email trust model .

section.name: HTTPS Execution Profile
section.t: The client sends an authenticated POST using HTTP semantics with Content-Type: application/json to the execution URL. The JSON body conforms to the request definition in the MAP schema. Service authentication and OAuth security follow the service's established configuration and applicable guidance such as .

A successful response uses application/json. The service returns status 200 for the terminal accepted, completed, or failed states, and status 202 for the non-terminal pending or approval-required states. A failed result reports work that the service previously accepted but could not complete; a request rejected before acceptance uses a Problem Details response. Every response carries a Location header for the request's result resource and repeats the exact type and target references.

Errors use application/problem+json . MAP 0.1 defines invalid-request, authentication-required, refused, result-not-found, stale-target, expired-interaction, unsupported-profile, unsupported-type, unsupported-operation, idempotency-conflict, and request-in-progress. A service MUST NOT apply the requested effect when returning one of these problems.

section.name: Idempotency and Recovery
section.t: A client generates a UUID URN as requestId. The service establishes the tenant and principal from its authenticated transport context, not from request fields. Within that scope, the first use binds the identifier to the complete JSON request value. Repeating the identifier with the same JSON values is an exact retry. The service MUST recheck current authorization, then return the latest recorded response without applying the effect again. Object member order is insignificant; array order and member values are significant. An implementation can use the JSON Canonicalization Scheme when deriving a request digest.
When the same interaction is redelivered and a client has already prepared the same operation and input, the client MUST reuse its complete persisted request, including its requestId.
Reuse with a changed value produces an idempotency-conflict. The changed request MUST NOT be applied.

Request claiming, effect initiation, and recoverable state MUST be atomic, or the service MUST reconcile an interrupted operation without repeating the business effect. A non-terminal result can advance to one terminal result; a terminal result MUST NOT advance.

A malformed request or request for an unknown interaction MUST NOT claim its identifier. A syntactically valid request for a recognized interaction and authenticated principal is claimed before type-specific input validation. Its type-validation failure is recoverable, and a corrected body uses a new identifier. For every claimed request, the service MUST isolate an existing identifier to its original principal and check current authorization before disclosing saved state. A new identifier is claimed before an effect begins, and its first recoverable outcome, including a permission refusal or type-validation failure, is recorded with that claim. This specification does not require a total precedence among independent validation failures.

An authenticated GET to the result resource rechecks current authorization and returns the latest recorded result or problem. After a timeout, a client SHOULD retrieve that resource before issuing a request that might repeat the effect. An uncertain outcome is local client state; it is not a MAP result value.

The advertised retention interval begins when the first response is recorded. A service MUST preserve enough duplicate suppression state after result disclosure ends to prevent the same scoped request identifier from applying the effect again.
A result-not-found problem identifies the requested requestId. When the service has no known interaction for that identifier, it MUST NOT invent an interactionId.

section.name: Interaction Types
section.t: MAP separates the execution profile from interaction semantics. A type contract defines the target semantics, stable operations, required inputs, and normal results. A description binds the type URI, version, and SHA-256 digest of that complete contract serialized with the JSON Canonicalization Scheme . Implementations do not guess compatibility.
A Registry record can add discovery metadata, maintainers, examples, evidence, and history without changing the wire contract. Registry lookup is not required during an interaction.

The initial Content Review 0.2 type offers request-changes and approve for an exact content revision. Approval records a review decision; it does not send or publish the content. A proposed approval can complete as approved or fail as declined, stale, or expired. A service authorizes the human decision separately from the proposing request; a different authorized principal in the same tenant can make that decision.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Implementations must treat structured content as attacker-controlled. The endpoint trust checks in prevent an email from redirecting a service credential. Schema validation does not establish trust or permission.

Services must protect result resources with current authorization equivalent to the underlying operation, including on exact retry. Error detail should disclose no token, private target content, or permission information beyond what the caller is allowed to know.
A target revision and digest prevent an approval from silently moving to changed content. Services must compare the request with current target state before applying an effect.

Clients should present the operation, target, scope, and consequence before obtaining human approval. A changed target or materially changed action requires a new decision according to service policy.

A service can grant a caller no approval authority, proposal authority that produces approval-required, or delegated authority that can produce completed. The protocol does not infer authority from whether the caller is a person or an automated client.
The service must authorize a human approval decision against current tenant, role, target, and expiry state. An unauthorized decision attempt does not change the saved non-terminal result.

section.name: Privacy Considerations
section.t: Descriptions are carried through email systems and may be retained or forwarded. They should contain the minimum target metadata needed to understand the action. Sensitive source material should remain behind an authorized service route rather than being copied into the description.
Result retention is advertised in seconds. A service must retain the result for at least that interval and should not retain it longer than its stated service purpose requires.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document requests no IANA action. MAP 0.1 uses existing media types and HTTPS. A future version that introduces a new media type or well-known URI will define the required registration.

section.name: Implementation Status
section.t: This section follows and may be removed before publication as an RFC.

The MailSchema repository contains digest-bound JSON Schemas, valid and invalid fixtures, a complete MIME message, a deterministic client/service harness, a requirement matrix, and conformance cases for completion, refusal, stale targets, approval, exact retry, conflict, recovery, expiry, unsupported contracts, and untrusted endpoints. JavaScript, Python, Rust, and Go packages expose the schemas. The materials are available at .

Nitrosend has an implementation of partial-representation MIME generation and inbound description extraction. An authenticated Content Review service implementation, durable retry and recovery storage, and its OpenAPI contract are under test. No deployed end-to-end conformance result or independent implementation is claimed. MailSchema and Nitrosend share ownership.
